content.title: What is Connection Pooling?
content.description: Connection Pooling is a technique that maintains a pool of reusable database connections. Instead of creating a new connection for every database request, applications borrow a connection from the pool and return it after use.

content.content: Creating a new database connection is an expensive operation because it involves network communication, authentication, and resource allocation. Connection Pooling improves application performance by creating a limited number of reusable database connections that can be shared among multiple requests.

content.title: Why Connection Pooling?
content.content: Connection pooling reduces the overhead of repeatedly creating and closing database connections, resulting in faster response times and better resource utilization.

A connection pool initializes several database connections when the application starts. Whenever a database operation is needed, an available connection is borrowed from the pool and returned after use instead of being destroyed.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Connections are reused instead of recreated, significantly improving the performance of database-driven applications.

content.content: Most Java applications use a DataSource implementation provided by a connection pooling library to obtain pooled database connections.

content.title: Important
content.content: Closing a pooled connection does not destroy it. Instead, the connection is returned to the pool for reuse.

content.title: Car Rental Service
content.content: Imagine a car rental company with a fleet of cars. Customers borrow a car, use it, and return it when finished. The cars are reused by other customers instead of buying a new car for every trip. Connection pooling works in the same way with database connections.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Connection pooling, DataSource, HikariCP, Apache DBCP, connection reuse, maximum pool size, connection timeout, idle timeout, and database performance optimization are among the most frequently asked JDBC interview topics.

items.question: Should pooled connections always be closed?
items.answer: Yes. Calling close() returns the connection to the pool instead of permanently closing it.

items.question: Is creating a very large pool always beneficial?
items.answer: No. Excessively large pools waste resources and may overload the database server.

items.question: Should DriverManager be used for every database request in production?
items.answer: No. Modern enterprise applications typically use DataSource with connection pooling.
